title: Catch one excuse before it replaces an honest response

sections.title: Understand the distinction
sections.body: Self-deception substitutes a convenient account for a checkable one. Perfectionistic delay endlessly polishes sufficient work; blame ignores one’s available action; control disguises preference as necessity; withdrawal avoids a safe owed response; intellectualization discusses principles instead of the concrete task; performative humility seeks reassurance instead of correction. These are hypotheses about behavior, not diagnoses or proof of hidden motives.

sections.title: Complete fictional practice material
sections.body: Request received 09:00: “Can you attend the optional planning call Friday 14:00? Please answer by 16:00 today.” Jo knows a prior appointment conflicts. Draft at 10:00: “Thank you; I cannot attend Friday 14:00.” Jo rewrites it six times without adding information. No safety, privacy or access barrier is supplied.

sections.title: Work through the supplied case
sections.body: Identify the narrow observable problem, an alternative explanation you would check in a real case, and a truthful response. Do not infer character from one delay.

sections.title: Try a different case before checking
sections.body: A person says “I am so useless; reassure me” after a correctable typo, but never checks the correction. What task-focused response would help?

checks.title: Compare reasoning and review the supplied result
checks.body: The draft already answers accurately; send it through the normal route or state a real newly discovered constraint. Later fiction: Jo sends 10:10, still feels awkward, and receives no reply. Partial: recognize delay but keep rewriting. Incorrect: blame the recipient for an unreadable request or invent attendance. For another pattern, pick its observable cue and an equally concrete honest alternative; do not label every hesitation avoidance.
criteria: Observable behavior is separated from motive claims
The honest alternative addresses the actual request

checks.title: Check the changed case
checks.body: Acknowledge the feeling without endorsing the global verdict; check and correct the typo, with proportionate responsibility. Reassurance alone does not perform the correction, and one exchange does not prove a personality pattern.
